item: Row 405 (R824 step 1): the carry records each stage's version and where carried rows came from, a golden-corpus output digest polices the versions, and an import says which part of the engine differed
key_paths: src/analytics/engine_identity.py; src/analytics/store.py; src/analytics/golden_output.py; src/backup/merge.py; src/backup/import_reports.py; src/static/app-backup.js; scripts/indexer_pin.py; configs/extraction_digests.json; migrations/versions/e4b7c1d9a2f6_stage_versions_and_engine_registry.py; tests/test_stage_version_carry_r824.py; tests/test_extraction_golden_output.py; tests/fixtures/extraction_golden/
summary: Built on R412/R415, which had already replaced the byte-hash engine id with the hand-bumped INDEXER_VERSION / WWW_INDEXER_VERSION (the proposal's 18-hour churn figure predates them), so no new constant and no version bump: STAGE_VERSIONS reads the two. Additive schema (R755 F2): nullable stage_version and carried_from_batch on article_index_stamps and article_www_stamps, and index_engines (engine id, stage, the components JSON the id is a hash of). index_article writes the stage version, clears carried_from_batch and records its engine; the carry writes this machine's version and the batch, refuses a stamp whose recorded version is another or not a number (R824 addition 3; NULL, a stamp from before the column, still carries through its engine id, which hashes the version), and its plan names every engine part an incoming stamp differs in with article counts, from the backup's index_engines rows that recompute to their own id, and counts the rest as could not be read; names come from this machine's record only, never from the backup's text. The import report gains an 'Extraction reused from the backup' section in plain words; the re-index backlog gives carried, extracted here, not recorded (a stamp older than the record) and awaiting per stage, shown under the import's analytics statement (3 strings x12, label-and-value form); the carry also records this machine's own engine rows. A 207-article golden corpus covering the scripts of the 12 UI languages gives each stage an output digest (configs/extraction_digests.json) recorded in the requirements.lock environment (dictionaries, switches, Python, Unicode and any install-generated gazetteer; the repository's own data files are judged by the digest itself) and checked, never skipped, in CI's lockfile-install job (not yet a required check of the branch ruleset: the maintainer's click); indexer_pin.py --same refuses when the output changed or the environment differs, and --bump refuses outside that environment before writing anything. The machine components (dictionaries, switches, Python, Unicode) and per-install gazetteer hashes stay in the identity: they narrow the carry, never widen it. The user's backups made before this gain nothing from it (they predate the record); the diagnostic is what says why a carry did not fire.
